questions.q: Describe the major physiographic divisions of India.
answer: India can be divided into six major physiographic divisions.

answer.text: Young fold mountains in the north, made of three ranges — the Himadri or Great Himalayas with the highest peaks, the Himachal or Middle Himalayas, and the outer Shivaliks with their Dun valleys.
Flat, fertile land formed by the alluvium of the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra.
The oldest landmass, made of the Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau, bordered by the higher, continuous Western Ghats and the lower, broken Eastern Ghats.
The Thar Desert in the north-west, the western and eastern Coastal Plains, and the coral Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

questions.q: Distinguish between the Western and Eastern Ghats.
answer: The Peninsular Plateau is bordered by two ranges of hills, the Western and Eastern Ghats, which differ in several ways.

answer.text: They run continuously along the western edge of the Deccan, are higher, and can be crossed only through passes. Their highest peak is Anai Mudi. They cause heavy rainfall on the western side by forcing the monsoon winds to rise, and are a source of many rivers.
They run along the eastern edge, are lower and discontinuous, being broken by the many rivers of the peninsula that flow into the Bay of Bengal.
The two ranges meet in the south at the Nilgiri Hills.
